_comment: Grok Build 1.0.13 (5e9a58528b76) native plan mode, captured live on
temp cwd holding a README.md, with comet's own initialize (fs + terminal
capabilities declined). Every frame below is verbatim from that session.
to these shapes; the fake agent in fake-acp.sh replays them.

session_new_result._comment: No `modes` key at all — plan mode is accepted but unadvertised. Trimmed to the keys the adapter reads.

current_mode_update_default._comment: The non-plan mode id, live-verified: `set_mode {"modeId":"default"}` → `{}` and this report. Unknown ids (normal, build, code, auto, ask) are answered `{}` with NO current_mode_update — the mode does not change.

plan_file_edit._comment: The plan is a real file the agent edits with search_replace: ~/.grok/sessions/<percent-encoded-cwd>/<session-id>/plan.md. `session/load` later replays current_mode_update with the persisted mode, so plan mode survives a reconnect.

content.newText:
Rename README.md to README2.md in the workspace.
Use a git mv or filesystem rename; do not change file contents.

exit_tool_call_update._comment: The opening call and this update carry NO plan text — the plan reaches the client on the gate request below.

pending_interaction._comment: grok's extension channel announces the gate just before raising it.

exit_gate_request._comment: THE EXIT GATE. Not `session/request_permission`: a grok extension reverse request (ExitPlanModeExtRequest, 3 fields). Answering it with a JSON-RPC error (-32601) yields the tool result "Plan approval could not be completed because the client disconnected. Plan mode remains active…" and cancels the turn (`stopReason: cancelled`, `cancellationCategory: PermissionCancelled`).

params.planContent:
Rename README.md to README2.md in the workspace.
Use a git mv or filesystem rename; do not change file contents.

exit_gate_response_keep_planning._comment: ExitPlanModeExtResponse has 2 fields; `approved` is one and `abandoned` is the other reading of the binary's TUI branches (approve / request changes / abandon). Unknown fields are IGNORED, so this superset is accepted verbatim — verified live. `feedback` is NOT the second field: sending it still selected the no-feedback branch, so the adapter only REJECTS the gate — the engine delivers the feedback as the user's next message through the ordinary steer path (ARCHITECTURE §11.2).

content.text: The user wants to revise the plan. Ask the user what changes they would like to make.

_comment: grok's ask-the-user extension, captured live on the same session. A
reverse request, not session/request_permission: options carry
{label, description} and `multiSelect` is null for a single pick. The
same tool also streams as tool_call/tool_call_update with

questions.question: Which color do you prefer, red or blue?

_comment: The reply that makes the tool succeed (UserAnswered): answers are keyed
by the QUESTION TEXT, the value is the picked label — an array of labels
when multiSelect is true, a string otherwise (the keying Claude's
AskUserQuestion uses). AskUserQuestionExtResponse is internally tagged:
a reply without `outcome` fails the tool with "missing field `outcome`".

unverified: The APPROVE path (`approved: true`) was not exercised live — it would have let the agent edit the workspace. The response shape is the same object.

The exact name of ExitPlanModeExtResponse's second field: `abandoned` is inferred from the binary's TUI branches; `feedback` was ruled out live. Sending `{approved, abandoned}` works because unknown fields are ignored and `approved` is honored.
Whether grok will ever raise the gate as a plain `session/request_permission`. The adapter handles that shape too, gated on the reported plan mode.

The names of AskUserQuestionExtResponse's non-`Accepted` variants: only `accepted` was exercised, so a dropped resolver answers `{"outcome":"accepted","answers":{}}` rather than guessing a cancel variant.
The multiSelect:true wire (an array of labels) is the mirror of Claude's AskUserQuestion answer shape; grok raised only single-select questions live.
